title: Report looks at reasons for Vogtle construction delays
html:
A lack of a realistic schedule; a failure to adhere to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission’s quality assurance requirements; and changes to Westinghouse’s AP1000 incomplete reactor design during construction were the primary reasons Vogtle-3 and -4 suffered delays, a new report says.

Columbia University’s Center on Global Energy Policy (CGEP) issued its report, “Insights into Construction Delays at the Vogtle Nuclear Plant: Primary Sources of Delay Identified by the Independent Construction Monitor,” on November 15. This report investigated the delays that ultimately made the country’s most recent commercial reactor project a costly affair and outlined the lessons learned that current and future projects can take from Vogtle.
